scientific_question: Do paired causal intervention responses from epistemically distinct biological-evidence and observability-risk channels identify hidden failure classes across mechanism-subtype shift more reliably and with fewer experiments than event-only, observability-only, or early scalar fusion?
scientific_object: causal experiment selection and failure identification, not a new sensing-allocation score

semantics.placebo: matched repeat with no causal repair; used only as the response reference and not counted against the active budget
semantics.event_restore: intervene on the event-evidence path while leaving the observability path structurally unchanged
semantics.observability_restore: intervene on the observability-risk path while leaving the event-evidence path structurally unchanged
semantics.shared_restore: intervene on a shared representation path that can affect both observer channels

protected_random_audit.reveals: fault_present only; it never reveals the causal failure class

common_diagnostic_algorithm.training: class-conditional intervention-response centroids estimated only from development mechanism subtypes
common_diagnostic_algorithm.scaling: feature-wise mean/std learned only on development responses; zero-variance scale set to one
common_diagnostic_algorithm.step_1_intervention: choose the active intervention with the largest minimum pairwise development-centroid separation across all four failure classes
common_diagnostic_algorithm.after_each_observation: rank classes by squared Euclidean distance on only the interventions already observed
common_diagnostic_algorithm.next_intervention: take the two currently nearest class hypotheses and choose the remaining intervention with the largest development-centroid separation between those two hypotheses
common_diagnostic_algorithm.final_diagnosis: nearest development centroid after two active interventions
common_diagnostic_algorithm.full_battery_ceiling: nearest development centroid after all three active interventions

A.allowed_claim: Paired causal interventions combined with distinct observer channels materially improve held-out failure identification and repair selection over the tested single-channel and early-fusion representations.

B.allowed_claim: Causal intervention responses make the distinct-channel development strategy competitive overall and improve shared-failure diagnosis conditionally.

C.allowed_claim: Interventional diagnosis has mixed or mechanism-specific value; report identifiability boundaries without a general superiority claim.

requirements: interventional_dual_observer budget2 localisation < best comparator - 0.05 OR interventional_dual_observer shared recall < 0.50
D.allowed_claim: Even under controlled interventions, the tested distinct-channel representation does not improve reliable held-out failure identification over simpler representations.

forbidden_claims: V12 changes V7 or V11 outcomes
simulation interventions substitute for blinded physical intervention blocks
